articles.title: Ashton Jeanty’s cryptic post sparks injury concerns among Las Vegas Raiders fans
articles.standfirst: The Raiders are waiting for answers, but Jeanty’s latest message has everyone talking.
articles.summary: The Raiders are waiting for answers, but Jeanty’s latest message has everyone talking.
articles.body:
The entire Las Vegas Raiders fan base held its breath recently after it was revealed that running back Ashton Jeanty had to be helped off the field after suffering a leg injury during practice. At first, many feared the worst and even thought he could miss the entire season.

The Raiders have yet to officially confirm the severity of the injury, although multiple reports indicate that Jeanty suffered only an ankle sprain . While the injury could force him to miss some games, it is not expected to threaten his season.

The running back has not spoken publicly about what happened, but he did share a cryptic message on Instagram. Jeanty posted a photo of himself kneeling alongside the Bible verse Romans 8:28.

“And we know that in all things God works for the good of those who love him, who have been called according to his purpose,” the verse reads.

It remains unclear what Jeanty intended to convey with the message. It could be interpreted as thanking God for helping him avoid a more serious injury, or as a sign of faith that even this setback is part of a greater purpose. What is certain is that his return timeline will depend on the Raiders’ final evaluation.

Klint Kubiak provides positive update on Jeanty

Raiders head coach Klint Kubiak typically does not reveal many details about injuries, but his comments regarding Jeanty provided an encouraging sign.

“Again, Ashton got hurt in practice, and the whole team took a knee. That says a lot about him being on the mend and counting on him,” Kubiak told reporters. “Really excited about getting him back. I’m a huge believer in the power of prayer.”

Jeanty enters this season with high expectations after being selected in the Top 10 of the Draft and being considered one of the most talented running backs to come out of college in recent years . His impact will be crucial for a Las Vegas offense that could face major challenges if it is forced to move forward without its top weapon in the running game.

articles.title: Tom Brady secured a Fernando Mendoza relic that could be worth massive amount of money in the future
articles.standfirst: Brady wasn't going to let this potential piece of history slip away from his grasp.
articles.summary: Brady wasn't going to let this potential piece of history slip away from his grasp.
articles.body:
It's a truly new and fresh era for the Las Vegas Raiders . Heading into the 2026 season, the team has a new head coach in Klint Kubiak , several new faces on the roster, and their franchise quarterback of the future in Fernando Mendoza .

While general manager John Spytek did most of the dirty work, Tom Brady has surely helped plenty behind the scenes. The minority owner has been a constant presence, whenever he's not on Fox Sports duty, and is hoping to leave his mark on the organization. Brady is also hoping Mendoza leaves his own mark over the course of his NFL career .

Brady surely signed off on the Mendoza pick, as the Raiders front office likely wanted input from the GOAT quarterback when it came to selecting the franchise's new QB of the future. It's clear that Brady has high hopes for Mendoza, especially after Brady pulled off a stunning move for a piece of Mendoza memorabilia .

Tom Brady paid "life-altering amount of money" for Fernando Mendoza rookie card

Last month, Brady splashed the cash for a rare 1-of-1 Mendoza rookie card, which featured the rookie's signature and the caption "My 1st NFL Auto" on the card. As it turns out, Brady paid a pretty penny for it. One of Brady's business partners, Chris Costa , revealed recently that the former QB paid a " life-altering amount of money for most people " in order to get the card.

Costa says that Brady was dying to get his hands on the card, since it was as rare as a card can get - only one exists in the world: " Tom basically raised his hand and was like, ‘I want that card. I need that card.' ” Brady got it, but his wallet took a hit in the process. Thankfully, as long as Mendoza's NFL career pans out as expected, that card could be worth a fortune in the future.

articles.title: Where to watch Raiders vs 49ers and What time does the NFL preseason game start?
articles.standfirst: In the final week of preparation, the Raiders host San Francisco for a final test
articles.summary: In the final week of preparation, the Raiders host San Francisco for a final test
articles.body:
The NFL preseason always brings with it a different feel: less pressure on the scoreboard, more opportunities for rookies, and a showcase for coaching staffs that are still putting together their 53-man rosters. This matchup between the Las Vegas Raiders and the San Francisco 49ers fits that mold perfectly. It is a meeting between two organizations that share history in the Bay Area and that now measure their backups and those fighting for a spot on the final roster.

Before we dive headlong into the betting markets, the context must be made clear: this is an NFL Preseason 2026 game, where the result matters much less than the internal evaluations .

Las Vegas Raiders vs San Francisco 49ers: What time does the game start and where can you watch it?

The opening whistle for the matchup between San Francisco and Las Vegas is scheduled for this Thursday, August 27, 2026 at 8:00 p.m. Eastern Time. The venue will be Allegiant Stadium, in the city of Las Vegas, United States, an arena with a capacity of about 65,000 spectators and home of the Raiders.

For the rest of the United States, the game will be at:

The Raiders are the home team, so the setting will be the usual Las Vegas atmosphere, although in the preseason the stands rarely look packed . Even so, Allegiant Stadium always offers a striking backdrop to kick off the campaign.

As for the game broadcast, you can watch the game live locally on FOX5 if you're in Las Vegas, and KPIX 5 and CW if you're in San Francisco. Streaming-wise, the game between the Raiders and 49ers will be available on NFL+.

What you need to know about the preseason if you're entering the betting market for this Raiders vs 49ers game

Unlike the regular season, an August game does not award points that count toward the AFC or NFC standings . There are no seeding or division implications.

What there is, though, is valuable information for bettors: how much the starters play, who leads the opening drives, and how aggressive each coaching staff is with its key players.

That is the most decisive factor of all. In these matchups, one team can win 20-3 with an inspired second unit, while another can lose even though its ideal starting eleven looks superior on paper.

The starting talent almost never decides the outcome of a preseason game ; it is decided by bench depth and rotation decisions.

The key, in short, is to bet small and bet on what the preseason really rewards: discipline, roster depth, and low-scoring games , rather than the reputation of stars who will barely set foot on the gridiron.

articles.title: Curt Cignetti says Fernando Mendoza’s Raiders success may be out of his hands
articles.standfirst: The Indiana coach believes Mendoza has everything needed to succeed, but Las Vegas must give him enough support.
articles.summary: The Indiana coach believes Mendoza has everything needed to succeed, but Las Vegas must give him enough support.
articles.body:
Expectations surrounding Fernando Mendoza couldn't be much higher after the Las Vegas Raiders used the first overall selection in the 2026 NFL Draft on the former Indiana quarterback.

But Curt Cignetti , who coached Mendoza during his remarkable college rise, believes judging the rookie purely on his own performances would ignore how dependent any quarterback is on the players around him.

“Well, I think he’s got the tools, and mentally, he’s extremely smart, dedicated, committed, does everything he can to be the best he can be, a great teammate, and a great leader,” Cignetti told NFL on ESPN.

“He’s a great competitor on the field. He’s got a quick arm; he’s got good arm strength, and he’s got good mobility. So, he’s got a body of work out there, and he’s going to be a really good pro.”

Cignetti highlights what Mendoza needs from Raiders

The bigger uncertainty for Cignetti isn't whether Mendoza possesses NFL quality, but whether Las Vegas can create the conditions necessary for him to show it immediately.

“People ask me, ‘How do you think he’s going to do this year?’ I said, ‘Well, I don’t know a whole lot about the Raiders, to be honest with you,’” Cignetti said.

“You know, you’ve got to have protection. You’ve got to have guys that can separate. You’ve got to have a run game. You’ve got to be able to play defense and special teams. It all goes hand in hand.”

That supporting cast could become particularly important following an uneven start to Mendoza's pro career .

Fernando Mendoza facing pressure after preseason struggles

Across his first two preseason appearances, Mendoza completed 18 of 31 passes, while taking two sacks and throwing one interception.

His numbers when pressured have attracted particular attention, with the rookie ranking near the bottom of preseason quarterbacks in both EPA per attempt and completion percentage under pressure.

It's a significant change from the environment Mendoza enjoyed at Indiana, where strong protection, dependable offensive weapons and an effective defense helped him flourish on his way to becoming college football's standout player.

That means his early fortunes in Las Vegas could depend heavily on whether the Raiders can keep him protected and provide enough offensive support.

Cignetti , though, remains convinced that even if success doesn't arrive immediately, his former quarterback will eventually establish himself.

“But he’s going to be a good pro if not this year, sometime soon,” he said.

articles.title: “Looking for 25 year olds”: Tom Brady ripped for using GQ makeover to hide deep insecurities
articles.summary: Jason Whitlock has taken aim at Tom Brady over the former NFL quarterback’s latest GQ appearance.
articles.body:
Jason Whitlock has taken aim at Tom Brady over the former NFL quarterback’s latest GQ appearance.

The seven-time Super Bowl champion recently appeared in a fashion-focused campaign, showing a different side of himself years after leaving the New England Patriots .

Whitlock wasn’t impressed and used the shoot as the basis for a wider criticism of Brady’s public image and personality.

"Tom Brady continues his transformation into becoming a woke leftist," Whitlock captioned, not really understanding what 'woke' means, like most people who use it.

Whitlock questions Brady's motivation

Whitlock argued that Brady’s fashion makeover was about more than simply appearing in a magazine campaign.

"He's trying to tell 25-year-old women, 'hey, I'm still relatable.' I think Tom Brady has insecurity issues," Whitlock said. "We thought he was this humble kid from Michigan. No, this is a guy from Northern California who perhaps is being who he was always going to be, and that Bill Belichick pushed that out of him while he was with the Patriots

The comments represented a sharp attack on the image Brady cultivated during his long career in New England, where he became closely associated with Bill Belichick and the Patriots ’ disciplined culture.

Whitlock suggested that Brady’s personality has changed significantly since leaving the franchise, although his interpretation was presented as opinion rather than evidence of Brady’s own motivations.

Brady's post NFL image comes under fire

Brady has remained highly visible since retiring from football, moving into broadcasting while also appearing regularly in advertising and fashion campaigns.

That visibility has brought plenty of scrutiny, particularly as the 49-year-old has embraced a more fashion-conscious image than fans were accustomed to during his playing career.

Whitlock believes that shift reflects a bigger change.

"As soon as he left Bill Belichick, Tom Brady feels a bit more comfortable being exactly who he is: a Northern Californian leftist."

Brady hasn’t publicly responded to Whitlock’s criticism.

The former quarterback has faced plenty of commentary about his appearance and lifestyle since retirement, but his GQ campaign appears to have triggered a particularly personal response from Whitlock .

articles.title: Grand opening disaster: Tom Brady hit by $12,000 theft in Palo Alto just one week after launch
articles.standfirst: Tom Brady’s new trading card store was burglarized just one week after opening in Palo Alto.
articles.summary: Tom Brady’s new trading card store was burglarized just one week after opening in Palo Alto.
articles.body:
Tom Brady has suffered an early setback with his latest business venture after thieves targeted his newly opened trading card store in California.

The store, CardVault by Tom Brady , was burglarized in Palo Alto only days after its grand opening, with authorities estimating that around $12,000 worth of merchandise was stolen.

The incident reportedly happened during the early hours of August 24, when suspects broke into the business and removed a number of valuable items before fleeing.

For Brady , the timing could hardly have been worse after the seven-time Super Bowl champion had only recently celebrated the launch of the location.

Thieves target Brady’s new store

The Palo Alto Police Department said officers responded after receiving a report of a commercial burglary at the store.

Investigators believe the suspects entered the property overnight and stole merchandise valued at approximately $12,000.

The items taken reportedly included collectible trading cards, which can carry significant value depending on their rarity and condition.

No injuries were reported in connection with the burglary, and the suspects had already left the scene by the time police arrived.

Authorities are continuing to investigate the incident as they attempt to identify those responsible.

Store had only just opened

CardVault by Tom Brady officially opened its Palo Alto location only around a week before the burglary.

The business is part of Brady’s growing collection of ventures away from football and focuses on sports cards, memorabilia and other collectibles.

Brady became involved with CardVault as both an investor and partner, attaching his name to a company aimed at expanding in the increasingly valuable sports memorabilia market.

The Palo Alto store had been promoted as another step in that expansion, making the burglary an unwelcome interruption almost immediately after its debut.

Brady has not publicly commented on the theft.

While the reported financial loss is relatively small compared with the former quarterback’s broader business empire, the incident represents an unfortunate start for the new location.

Police have not yet announced any arrests , and the investigation remains ongoing as officials work to determine exactly how the burglary was carried out and where the stolen merchandise may have gone.

articles.title: Question marks raised by Fernando Mendoza after latest loss cast doubt on choice made by Tom Brady and prove Klint Kubiak right
articles.standfirst: The rookie struggled again as Kubiak suggested he still needs more time before taking over
articles.summary: The rookie struggled again as Kubiak suggested he still needs more time before taking over
articles.body:
The Raiders don't have to say Fernando Mendoza is headed for the bench to make the picture clear as Thursday’s preseason finale against the San Francisco 49ers did that for them.

Kirk Cousins opened the game, moved Las Vegas into scoring position on both of his possessions and avoided the kind of mistake that can cost a quarterback a starting job.

Mendoza followed with a much more uneven night, finishing 7 of 14 for 57 yards while throwing his second interception in as many preseason games.

Coach Klint Kubiak ’s comments afterward may have said more than any depth chart could.

“He needs another three preseason games,” Kubiak said of Mendoza. “All those rookies do. And now that the season’s starting, the practice reps get smaller and that’s just life. But, as coaches, we got to get them ready to play, keep developing them.”

That's hardly the language of a coach preparing to hand over the offense immediately. The Raiders brought in Cousins this offseason in large part to give Mendoza time, and Thursday reinforced why.

Cousins completed 8 of 11 passes for 51 yards and led two field-goal drives. He wasn't spectacular, but he was controlled and mistake-free.

Mendoza had a rougher assignment once Las Vegas turned increasingly to its backups.

Protection broke down, he was sacked twice and the offense struggled to generate anything consistently. His interception also came on a high throw intended for Jalen Nailor that still reached the receiver’s hands before being tipped into the arms of Tatum Bethune .

It wasn't entirely on Mendoza , but the result added to the evidence that he is still adapting to NFL speed and decision-making.

Mendoza understands why patience may be necessary

The rookie was candid afterward about the difficulty of the transition.

“The NFL is really tough, you know,” Mendoza said. “There is a big jump going from college to the NFL, and the speed in, there’s so many different aspects.”

He also made clear he would take as many developmental opportunities as possible.

“I would love unlimited games for development,” Mendoza said. “There are always struggles. It’s not always sunshine, sunshines and rainbows.”

Cousins , meanwhile, refused to claim the job publicly.

“It’s just up to coach,” Cousins said. “You just do the best you can with the opportunities you’re given, lead as well as you can, compete.”

The Raiders may still wait before announcing anything formally. But with the regular-season opener approaching, Thursday looked less like the continuation of a quarterback competition and more like confirmation of the original plan.

articles.standfirst: The unique collection spans a career unlike any other in NFL history
articles.summary: The unique collection spans a career unlike any other in NFL history
articles.body:
T om Brady's NFL legacy is built on numbers that may never be matched. Seven Super Bowl championships. Ten Super Bowl appearances. Five Super Bowl MVP awards. Countless comeback victories and record-setting performances.

But years after his final NFL season, the greatest quarterback in league history revealed that some of his most treasured memories are not trophies, rings, or game footage. They're text messages.

Brady recently shared that he has maintained a remarkably organized digital archive on his phone, creating a separate folder for each of his Super Bowl victories and saving the messages he received after every championship. "You know what's pretty cool, let me show you my phone," Brady said. "I have kept file folders. I file everything."

Preserving football's biggest moments

Brady explained that each folder contains congratulatory messages and personal notes sent to him following his Super Bowl triumphs. "I keep all the amazing messages that people sent me. I wanted to keep them as great memories," Tom said.

The collection spans a career unlike any other in NFL history. From his first championship with the New England Patriots following the 2001 season to his final title with the Tampa Bay Buccaneers nearly two decades later, Brady accumulated more Super Bowl victories than any franchise quarterback in league history.

Instead of allowing those moments to fade with time, he created a system to preserve the personal side of each achievement. "Congratulations and a lot of really cool ones over the years," Brady said. "It's such a special moment and you always want to remember."

The human side of greatness

Professional athletes often speak about championships in terms of preparation, sacrifice, and execution. Brady's comments offered a different perspective. The folders are not focused on statistics, highlight reels, or media coverage. They are centered on relationships.

Every championship generated messages from teammates, coaches, family members, friends, and colleagues. Over time, those conversations became a digital time capsule documenting some of the most important moments of his life.

For an athlete who spent more than two decades under an intense public spotlight, the messages likely provide a reminder of the people who experienced those victories alongside him. It is a surprisingly personal habit from someone often viewed through the lens of records and accomplishments.

A reflection of Brady's personality

The revelation also underscores a characteristic that helped define Brady's success throughout his career: organization. Teammates and coaches frequently described him as obsessive in his preparation. Whether studying film, managing his training routines, or maintaining detailed notes on opponents, Tom built a reputation for leaving little to chance.

Creating and maintaining separate folders for every Super Bowl fits that profile. What might seem excessive to some is simply another example of the disciplined approach that helped transform a sixth-round draft pick into the most accomplished quarterback the sport has ever seen.

Championship rings remain the most visible symbols of Brady's success. Yet his comments suggest that the memories he values most may not be physical awards at all. Instead, they are the messages that arrived in the hours and days after football's biggest games, the texts from people who shared in the joy of victory, celebrated years of hard work, and recognized the significance of those moments.

articles.title: Klint Kubiak remains silent on the Raiders' quarterback battle despite there being a clear favorite
articles.standfirst: Kubiak won't name his starter, but the Raiders' preseason reps tell a different story
articles.summary: Kubiak won't name his starter, but the Raiders' preseason reps tell a different story
articles.body:
Klint Kubiak doesn't appear to be in any rush to officially settle the Las Vegas Raiders' quarterback competition, even though everything that has happened throughout training camp and the preseason points toward Kirk Cousins.

The Raiders finished their preseason with an 18-12 loss to the San Francisco 49ers, but the result wasn't the biggest question coming out of the game. Attention immediately turned to who will take the first snap at quarterback when the regular season begins.

Kubiak was asked whether Cousins had done enough to earn the starting job. His answer was essentially the same as it has been throughout the competition, stating no decision will be announced yet.

"I still don't think we need to name anybody," Kubiak said. “We have a lot to talk about at a lot of positions, so we want to watch the film and talk about everything as a staff."

That may be frustrating for fans, but Kubiak's actions have painted a much clearer picture.

Cousins has consistently worked with the starting offense throughout training camp, while rookie Fernando Mendoza has received relatively few opportunities with the first team. That distinction has remained important as the preseason has progressed.

The veteran also received the most meaningful playing time in the preseason finale against San Francisco. Kubiak opened the game with his starting offense, and Cousins led the first two drives before giving way to Mendoza and the second-team players.

The decision to use Cousins with the starters has significance. Coaches don't typically give those snaps to a player they aren't seriously considering for the opening-day lineup. The performances themselves have only strengthened the case for Cousins .

Cousins played three preseason drives and helped the Raiders produce 13 points. He completed 13 of 17 passes for 101 yards and a touchdown, while avoiding both interceptions and sacks.

The evidence keeps pointing toward Cousins

Mendoza , meanwhile, has struggled to make a convincing case for taking over immediately. He finished the preseason completing 25 of 45 passes for 240 yards, one touchdown and two interceptions.

His final preseason appearance was particularly difficult. Mendoza threw an interception on his second play, was sacked twice and finished with only 57 passing yards on 7-of-14 passing.

Kubiak still seems determined not to close the door on his young quarterback. After the loss, the coach said he wished Mendoza had three more preseason games to continue developing. Mendoza agreed that the additional playing time would've helped.

That comment might actually provide a better indication of where the Raiders stand.

Mendoza appears to be viewed as a quarterback with considerable potential who needs time, while Cousins is the experienced option capable of running the offense immediately.

Kubiak's reluctance to name Cousins shouldn't necessarily be interpreted as uncertainty, as the first-year head coach may simply prefer keeping his plans private until the Raiders are ready to make their final roster decisions.

Unless something changes dramatically, though, the quarterback competition appears to have a clear favorite. Cousins has received the first-team repetitions, performed efficiently and handled the most important preseason snaps.

Kubiak may not be ready to say it publicly, but the Raiders' actions suggest Cousins is heading toward the starting job.

articles.title: Fernando Mendoza could still get even worse Raiders news nobody expected
articles.standfirst: The No. 1 pick could begin his NFL career as Las Vegas' third quarterback.
articles.summary: The No. 1 pick could begin his NFL career as Las Vegas' third quarterback.
articles.body:
Fernando Mendoza's difficult start with the Las Vegas Raiders could take another unexpected turn, with head coach Klint Kubiak refusing to guarantee that the first overall pick will even begin the season as the team's No. 2 quarterback.

Kirk Cousins is widely expected to start, but Mendoza is still competing with Aidan O'Connell for the backup role.

That leaves open the surprising possibility that one of the most prominent rookies in the 2026 NFL Draft could begin his professional career third on the depth chart.

Klint Kubiak refuses to guarantee Mendoza QB2 role

Kubiak was directly asked whether Mendoza or O'Connell would serve as the backup if Cousins opens the season as Las Vegas' starter.

“We’ve got three guys that are ready to play. It’s going to be some hard decisions on who’s 1, who’s 2. That’s not a decision we have to make today, but those are discussions that are ongoing,” Kubiak said.

The answer offered Mendoza no guarantees despite the enormous investment the Raiders made when selecting him with the first pick of the draft.

It would be highly unusual for a No. 1 overall quarterback to begin his rookie season as QB3, particularly when first picks are normally expected to either start immediately or sit directly behind an experienced veteran.

Mendoza could face longer wait than expected

The Raiders appear in no rush to put Mendoza on the field.

If Cousins takes the starting job and O'Connell is ultimately selected as his primary backup, Mendoza could remain on the sideline even if Las Vegas needs to make a quarterback change early in the season.

Kubiak's comments make clear that the hierarchy hasn't yet been finalized.

That creates another layer of uncertainty for Mendoza as his rookie season approaches.

Being asked to sit behind a veteran such as Cousins would already require patience from the first overall pick. Falling behind O'Connell as well would represent an even more surprising beginning.

For now, Mendoza hasn't officially been named QB3.

But Kubiak has made one thing clear: his draft status alone won't guarantee him the backup job.

articles.title: Tom Brady receives an interesting offer from a free-agent running back to replace Ashton Jeanty
articles.standfirst: Veteran running back opens door to potential Raiders reunion
articles.summary: Veteran running back opens door to potential Raiders reunion
articles.body:
Austin Ekeler’s free-agent wait could become interesting for the Las Vegas Raiders if Ashton Jeanty’s ankle injury keeps him sidelined or limits his availability for Week 1.

The veteran running back is healthy, available and still looking for his next NFL opportunity after becoming a free agent earlier this year.

Ekeler has reportedly drawn interest from teams, although nothing has developed into serious negotiations. However, the Raiders could present an appealing destination, particularly because of his connection to the Las Vegas area.

When asked about a potential move to the Raiders, Ekeler didn’t hide his interest. He acknowledged that playing for his hometown team would be a dream for his family while also explaining exactly what he could offer.

“I’m unemployed right now,” Ekeler replied to reporter Madyson Marie. “Being in my hometown now, now my hometown anyway, would be a dream for my family. I know that is the situation, right? We’ll have to see. How is Jeanty feeling? Do they need another guy?"

Jeanty injury gives Raiders another decision to make

Jeanty suffered an ankle injury during practice after diving for a low throw from quarterback Kirk Cousins.

The second-year running back couldn’t put weight on his right leg and needed assistance from trainers to leave the field, immediately raising concerns about his availability for the season opener against the Miami Dolphins.

Fortunately for Las Vegas, subsequent reports suggested the injury isn’t expected to be long-term. Head coach Klint Kubiak has continued to describe Jeanty as being “on the mend” while emphasizing that the Raiders are counting on him. Still, that doesn’t guarantee he’ll be ready for Week 1.

If Jeanty can’t play, or if the coaching staff decides to limit his workload, rookie Mike Washington Jr. could receive an expanded role. Washington has already taken first-team repetitions and impressed during the preseason, giving Las Vegas an internal option.

Ekeler , though, would provide extensive NFL experience and proven ability as a receiver out of the backfield.

During his 2024 season with Washington, Ekeler averaged 4.8 yards per carry and caught 35 passes for 366 yards. His receiving ability has been one of his biggest strengths throughout his career, and he became a dependable safety valve for Jayden Daniels during his time with the Commanders.

That versatility could be particularly valuable for a Raiders offense still working through questions at quarterback.

Whether Cousins or rookie Fernando Mendoza eventually leads the offense, having a veteran running back capable of protecting the quarterback and contributing on passing downs could provide some welcome stability.

Ekeler’s Achilles injury ended his 2025 season after only two games, but he has since been medically cleared. The question now is whether a team believes he can immediately return to his previous level.

There’s little reason for Las Vegas to panic while Jeanty’s injury remains manageable. Washington gives the team another option, and the Raiders clearly expect Jeanty to return. But if his ankle doesn’t respond as hoped, Ekeler’s offer could suddenly become much more appealing.

articles.standfirst: The sight of the NFL legend courtside generated excitement throughout the venue
articles.summary: The sight of the NFL legend courtside generated excitement throughout the venue
articles.body:
T om Brady has attended countless major sporting events throughout his life. Seven Super Bowl victories, Hall of Fame-worthy achievements, and a global profile have made the former NFL quarterback one of the most recognizable athletes on the planet. Yet even in retirement, Brady continues to command attention wherever he goes.

That was certainly the case during Nebraska volleyball's matchup against UNLV at the Players Era Volleyball Showcase in Las Vegas. Fans inside the arena quickly noticed a familiar face sitting courtside as Brady took in the action alongside his daughter, Vivian Lake Brady . The appearance immediately became one of the biggest talking points surrounding the event, creating a buzz that extended well beyond the volleyball community.

A surprise guest in Las Vegas

Las Vegas has long been known for attracting celebrities to major sporting events. From championship boxing matches and UFC cards to NBA Summer League games and NFL events , star sightings have become part of the city's sports culture. The Players Era Volleyball Showcase proved no exception. As Nebraska and UNLV took the court, cameras and fans identified Brady seated near the action.

The sight of the NFL legend courtside generated excitement throughout the venue, with many spectators eager to catch a glimpse of the player widely regarded as the greatest quarterback in football history. Brady's presence added another layer of attention to an event that has continued to grow in prominence.

A special visit with Nebraska stars

Before the match, Brady and his daughter spent time meeting members of the Nebraska volleyball program . Nebraska standout Harper Murray and head coach Dani Busboom Kelly were among those who had the opportunity to catch up with the former NFL superstar.

The interaction highlighted the growing crossover appeal of women's volleyball, which has experienced a surge in popularity over the past several years. Nebraska remains one of the sport's flagship programs, routinely drawing massive crowds and national attention. Having someone of Brady's stature in attendance only amplified the spotlight.

Supporting his daughter's athletic dreams

While Brady's presence naturally drew headlines, his daughter may have been one of the main reasons for the visit. Vivian Lake Brady has previously expressed interest in pursuing athletics at a high level and has reportedly mentioned her desire to play basketball in college.

Attending elite sporting events alongside his children has become a recurring theme for Brady since retiring from the NFL . Whether it involves football, basketball, volleyball, or other sports, he has frequently emphasized the importance of supporting their interests and exposing them to high-level competition.

Watching one of the nation's premier volleyball programs compete could have provided both inspiration and insight for a young athlete with collegiate aspirations of her own.

articles.title: Fernando Mendoza's future takes a turn following Raiders' decision regarding Aidan O'Connell
articles.standfirst: The No.1 pick remains Las Vegas’ future, but Klint Kubiak has refused to guarantee him backup job
articles.summary: The No.1 pick remains Las Vegas’ future, but Klint Kubiak has refused to guarantee him backup job
articles.body:
Fernando Mendoza is still the quarterback the Las Vegas Raiders hope will lead them for years. What is less certain, after an uneven preseason and one revealing comment from Klint Kubiak , is whether he's even second in line right now.

Las Vegas kept three quarterbacks on its 53-man roster, with Aidan O’Connell joining veteran starter Kirk Cousins and Mendoza .

That decision alone doesn't amount to a crisis for the No.1 overall pick, but it does suggest the Raiders aren't yet ready to clear a direct path from Cousins to their rookie.

Kubiak reinforced that uncertainty when he was asked about the depth chart.

“We have three guys that are ready to play,” Kubiak said. “And it's going to be some hard decisions on who's one, who's two, and that's not a decision that we have to make today. But those are discussions that are ongoing.”

That's hardly the kind of endorsement usually attached to a rookie selected first overall and expected to become the future of the franchise.

Cousins has handled the majority of first-team work and remains positioned to open the season as the starter. The more intriguing question is whether Mendoza has done enough to move ahead of O’Connell .

Final preseason audition failed to settle debate

His performance against the San Francisco 49ers offered both development and frustration.

Mendoza completed 7 of 14 passes for 57 yards, threw an interception and took two sacks. His struggles came largely in areas where the transition from college to the NFL can be particularly unforgiving.

“It's the NFL, there are monsters on the other side of the ball and you need to get the ball out quick,” Mendoza said afterward. “It teaches you, you need to play on time, and there's less margin for error.”

He added: “So I think it's a great experience having that heat and duress because diamonds are built under pressure.”

The Raiders can afford patience. Mendoza won the Heisman Trophy and a national championship in his only season at Indiana before becoming the first pick in April, but that pedigree doesn't eliminate the need for development.

His experience working under center was limited in college, and some of his preseason mistakes reflected that adjustment.

O’Connell’s place on roster matters

O’Connell ’s survival is significant because he gives Las Vegas an experienced alternative.

The 27-year-old has appeared in 21 games for the Raiders over the past three seasons, making him a safer short-term option if Cousins is unavailable and Mendoza isn't ready.

That doesn't mean Las Vegas has changed its long-term plan. Mendoza remains the franchise quarterback in waiting. The question is how quickly he gets there.

Kubiak ’s decision not to name him the clear No.2 is therefore more important than the three-quarterback roster itself.

The Raiders don't need Mendoza to start in September, but they need him to keep progressing. Right now, the message from Las Vegas isn't that he has failed, it's that he hasn't yet separated himself.

articles.title: Mysterious Adam Schefter text message changes Fernando Mendoza's future with the Raiders
articles.standfirst: Kirk Cousins remains the favorite to open the season, but the No.1 pick’s takeover could be closer than it looks
articles.summary: Kirk Cousins remains the favorite to open the season, but the No.1 pick’s takeover could be closer than it looks
articles.body:
The Las Vegas Raiders may begin the season with Kirk Cousins under center, but the franchise’s long-term quarterback plan is already casting a shadow over that decision.

Fernando Mendoza , the No.1 overall draft pick and presumed future face of the organization, is expected to start his rookie season on the bench.

According to ESPN insider Adam Schefter , however, that arrangement may not last as long as many expect.

“I was texting with somebody yesterday,” Schefter said on The Pat McAfee Show. “They’re like, ‘Sooner than you think.’ I’m like, really?”

Schefter didn't identify the source of the message and stopped short of saying Mendoza is about to replace Cousins immediately.

His own expectation remains that Las Vegas opens the year with the veteran.

“I still think it’s going to be Kirk,” Schefter said. “I’d be surprised if it was anybody else other than Kirk at this point in time. I think that’s the way it’s been trending all along.”

Cousins appears to have Week 1 edge

Cousins entered training camp with a clear advantage.

He has years of starting experience, was signed specifically to stabilize the position and has the benefit of working under first-year head coach Klint Kubiak , who has been reluctant to rush Mendoza into action.

Schefter believes that experience will matter early in the season.

“I think Cousins starts the opener against the Miami Dolphins,” he said. “I think they want to go into veteran early in the season when there are some tough games on the schedule.”

That approach would allow Mendoza to continue developing without immediately carrying the pressure attached to being the top pick in the draft.

The Raiders have also kept Aidan O’Connell on the 53-man roster, giving them three quarterbacks and even more flexibility if the depth chart changes.

Mendoza’s future role not in question

The bigger mystery isn't whether Mendoza eventually becomes the starter, it's when.

“There’s no doubt his time is coming,” Schefter said. “He’s going to be the starter. He’s going to be the face of the franchise. The question is how soon?”

That is what makes the anonymous text so intriguing. Las Vegas can talk about patience now, but NFL seasons rarely follow a clean plan.

An injury, a slow start or a stretch of poor offensive performances could accelerate Mendoza ’s timeline quickly.

At the same time, one bad game from Cousins wouldn't necessarily be enough to trigger a change.

The Raiders brought in a veteran precisely so they wouldn't have to throw Mendoza into the lineup before he is ready.

Still, the message Schefter received suggests the internal timetable may be shorter than it appears from the outside. Cousins may get the first snap, but Mendoza may not have to wait very long for his.

articles.title: Ashton Jeanty’s injury scare turns to total optimism ahead of Dolphins opener
articles.standfirst: Ashton Jeanty’s injury raised concerns in Las Vegas, but the Raiders expect their star running back back sooner than expected.
articles.summary: Ashton Jeanty’s injury raised concerns in Las Vegas, but the Raiders expect their star running back back sooner than expected.
articles.body:
The Las Vegas Raiders enter the 2026 season with one clear mission: to rise again after a disappointing 2025 campaign in which they hit rock bottom with the worst record in the NFL. To dramatically change the direction of the franchise, the front office hired Klint Kubiak as the new head coach and completely revamped its quarterback room with the signing of Kirk Cousins and the arrival of Fernando Mendoza , the No. 1 overall pick in the Draft.

Ashton Jeanty raises concerns, but the Raiders remain calm

Despite the major structural changes, Las Vegas’ success in a brutal AFC West will largely depend on whether its young stars can reach their full potential. Running back Ashton Jeanty and tight end Brock Bowers enter the season carrying high expectations after a 2025 campaign filled with mixed emotions, establishing themselves as the cornerstones of the team’s new offensive project.

However, Jeanty’s second season got off to a difficult start. The star running back suffered a sprained ankle during training camp, raising concerns about the severity of the injury. Despite the scare, his medical progress has been positive, and the outlook points toward a quicker-than-expected return during the regular season.

Raiders general manager John Spytek eased concerns by saying the organization is confident it will get its running back back on the field soon, leaving the door open for an early return.

“I expect him to be back as quick he can, maybe quicker than some people would expect. When that is, we'll see.”

Although Jeanty has remained sidelined from practices since August 23 , his rehabilitation progress in recent days has been notable. With the season opener set for September 13 against the Miami Dolphins , the running back faces a race against the clock with less than two weeks to try to be ready for Week 1 .

If he is not medically cleared, rookie Mike Washington Jr . emerges as the top option to carry the load in the running game. Washington impressed during the preseason and summer practices, earning the confidence of Kubiak’s coaching staff.

Still, the Raiders invested a Top 10 selection in the 2025 Draft for one undeniable reason: Jeanty’s game-changing ability. Las Vegas is hoping for the quick return of its star to help put one of the darkest seasons in recent franchise history behind them.

articles.title: Tom Brady-backed Kirk Cousins wins Raiders QB1 job over rookie Fernando Mendoza
articles.standfirst: Klint Kubiak has made his quarterback decision ahead of Las Vegas’ season opener against Miami
articles.summary: Klint Kubiak has made his quarterback decision ahead of Las Vegas’ season opener against Miami
articles.body:
The Las Vegas Raiders have finally ended the uncertainty at quarterback, and their decision says as much about Fernando Mendoza ’s development as it does about Kirk Cousins ’ experience.

Head coach Klint Kubiak confirmed Wednesday that Cousins will start the 2026 season under center, giving the veteran the Week 1 assignment against the Miami Dolphins on September 13.

The move was widely anticipated after Cousins handled most of the first-team work during camp, but Kubiak had resisted making anything official until now.

Mendoza , the No.1 overall draft pick and presumed long-term face of the franchise, will begin his rookie year behind him.

The choice doesn't change how highly Las Vegas views Mendoza . It does, however, underline the patience the Raiders have preached since drafting him.

Why the Raiders can afford to wait on Mendoza

Mendoza arrived in Las Vegas after a remarkable final college season, winning the Heisman Trophy and leading Indiana to a national championship.

His first NFL preseason brought flashes of that promise, but also the inevitable mistakes of a rookie adjusting to the speed of the professional game.

The clearest example came against San Francisco, when Mendoza completed 7 of 14 passes for 57 yards, threw an interception and took two sacks.

“It’s the NFL, there are monsters on the other side of the ball and you need to get the ball out quick,” Mendoza said afterward. “It teaches you, you need to play on time, and there's less margin for error.”

He then offered a line that summed up his approach to the learning curve: “Diamonds are built under pressure.”

Kubiak has repeatedly stressed that Mendoza needs repetitions rather than shortcuts. Earlier in the preseason, when asked what would help the rookie most, he gave a blunt answer... “Reps.”

That development will now continue without the pressure of immediately carrying the offense.

Tom Brady remains firmly in Mendoza’s corner

Raiders minority owner Tom Brady was an admirer of Mendoza long before Las Vegas selected him first overall.

“I love everything about his game,” Brady said after Mendoza won the Heisman Trophy. “His leadership is what stands out. His relatability to his teammates. He's overcome a lot of things in his career.”

Mendoza has since spoken about Brady ’s influence behind the scenes.

“Tom's given me a lot of advice - and I like to sometimes keep it close to the vest,” Mendoza said.

“He always says is that, hey, you're in your early 20s and making sure you do everything possible to be successful and, and to best serve your teammates and not let your teammates down.”

Cousins , entering his 15th NFL season, now gets the first chance to guide the Raiders after arriving in Las Vegas following two seasons with Atlanta.

Mendoza ’s turn still feels inevitable. The Raiders have simply decided there's no reason it has to come in Week 1.

articles.title: Maxx Crosby’s wife Rachel details early fears involving wild Raiders fanbase
articles.standfirst: First experience at the Oakland Coliseum was far more intimidating than expected
articles.summary: First experience at the Oakland Coliseum was far more intimidating than expected
articles.body:
Rachel Crosby is now a familiar face around the Las Vegas Raiders , but her introduction to Raider Nation came with considerably more nerves than confidence.

The wife of star defensive end Maxx Crosby recalled what it was like attending Raiders games during the franchise’s final years in Oakland, admitting the warnings she received beforehand made the atmosphere sound more intimidating than exciting.

“I was nervous, because everybody was like, ‘You have to wear black, make sure everyone’s with you, wear Raiders stuff, don’t talk to the fans’,” Crosby said in an interview published by the team. “So, I’m nervous as hell.”

That anxiety didn't last. Crosby said the experience ultimately turned into something she loved, and over time she became closely connected with a fan base that has embraced both her and her husband.

Remembering old Oakland atmosphere

Crosby ’s comments are especially revealing because her first experiences came at the Oakland-Alameda County Coliseum, where Raiders games developed a reputation for being among the NFL’s most intense.

The franchise has since moved to Allegiant Stadium in Las Vegas, but the identity of Raider Nation remains rooted in the years when Oakland crowds were known for their passion, elaborate costumes and hostility toward visiting teams.

That reputation was enough to make Crosby cautious before she ever stepped inside. Her experience, however, quickly changed her perception.

Rather than feeling unwelcome, she came to appreciate the energy surrounding the franchise while Maxx established himself as one of the most important players on the roster.

Crosby entered the league as a fourth-round pick in 2019 and has since developed into one of the NFL’s premier edge rushers, becoming synonymous with the relentless style Raiders fans traditionally admire.

Maxx Crosby at center of Las Vegas’ future

Rachel ’s story comes as her husband prepares for another significant season with Las Vegas.

The Raiders enter 2026 with questions surrounding the direction of their defense, including how new coordinator Rob Leonard will shape the unit and how much pressure will once again fall on Crosby to generate disruption up front.

His future also became a talking point during the offseason amid trade speculation, although he remains the centerpiece of the defense heading into the regular season.

That status has only strengthened the Crosby family’s connection with Raider Nation. What once felt intimidating to Rachel has become familiar territory.

The setting is different now. Allegiant Stadium has a more modern, entertainment-driven atmosphere and regularly attracts large numbers of visiting supporters, but the franchise’s fan culture remains one of the strongest in football.

Rachel Crosby experienced that intensity before the move to Las Vegas and remembers exactly how it felt walking into it for the first time.

articles.title: Now Fernando Mendoza faces the worst-case scenario heading into his rookie season
articles.standfirst: Fernando Mendoza will have to wait. The Raiders named Kirk Cousins their starter, and an ESPN analyst believes the veteran QB could hold the job longer than expected.
articles.summary: Fernando Mendoza will have to wait. The Raiders named Kirk Cousins their starter, and an ESPN analyst believes the veteran QB could hold the job longer than expected.
articles.body:
The Las Vegas Raiders made an important decision ahead of the start of the 2026 NFL season by naming Kirk Cousins their starting quarterback. The move means Fernando Mendoza , the No. 1 overall pick in the Draft, will have to wait for his opportunity from the sideline while continuing his transition to the professional level.

During the previous season with the Atlanta Falcons, Cousins played 302 passing snaps and posted a 75.0 PFF grade. The veteran quarterback finished with 1,721 passing yards, 10 touchdowns, and five interceptions , while also recording nine big-time throws and five turnover-worthy plays.

Although Cousins was initially expected to serve as a bridge quarterback while Mendoza developed, ESPN NFL analyst Booger McFarland believes the veteran could remain Las Vegas’ starter for much of the season.

“Cousins should be the starter. I think anytime that Tom Brady comes out and talks about how he likes to develop a quarterback, and we know what his imprint is on this organization, that’s what they’re going to do. I wouldn’t be surprised if we don’t see Fernando Mendoza until the bye week,” McFarland said during the September 2 edition of ‘NFL Live.’

“I think they’re going to bring this young quarterback along slowly. Let’s not forget, he only took four or five snaps under center in college. So, everything is new to him: lining up under center, taking the snap, executing play-action passes — everything is completely new.”

Fernando Mendoza will have time to develop without pressure

McFarland highlighted that the situation will allow Mendoza to learn the details of the position without the pressure of immediately taking over as the starter. With the Raiders’ bye week not scheduled until Week 13 , the rookie quarterback will have several months to gain experience and confidence.

“It would be foolish of us to think that he’s mastered that in four or five months,” McFarland added. “I think this is going to be Kirk Cousins’ job, barring injury, until at least the bye week. And regardless of what happens on the field, aside from injury, they’re going to play Kirk Cousins.”

“Realize that the Raiders are in this for the long haul. This is not about 2026. This is about 2027 and beyond. So you put Kirk Cousins out there, you let him start, and you move on from there.”

“You develop Fernando Mendoza at practice the way coaches develop quarterbacks at practice. That’s a key factor we don’t talk about enough. Yes, he’s not going to play, but what are you going to do to develop him during the week of practice?”

articles.title: Who is Harper Murray? The volleyball star that shared a warm embrace with Tom Brady
articles.standfirst: The Nebraska All-American’s family history helps explain her link to the seven-time Super Bowl champion
articles.summary: The Nebraska All-American’s family history helps explain her link to the seven-time Super Bowl champion
articles.body:
Tom Brady ’s trip to watch one of the biggest matches in women’s college volleyball was always likely to attract attention, but it was his pregame greeting with Nebraska standout Harper Murray that unexpectedly became the viral moment of the night.

Brady attended Nebraska’s matchup with Texas at T-Mobile Arena in Las Vegas alongside his 13-year-old daughter Vivian , who has developed her own interest in volleyball.

Before play began, Murray came over to speak with the pair and shared a warm embrace with the seven-time Super Bowl champion.

Photos and video of the greeting quickly spread across social media, with one clip attracting millions of views. The interaction prompted plenty of online commentary.

Murray later explained that she already knew Brady through their shared ties to Michigan.

“I know him through some Michigan connections and the football program and administration there,” Murray said, via Husker Corner.

That connection is deeply personal for the Nebraska star.

Harper Murray’s Michigan connection

Murray’s father, Vada Murray , played defensive back for Michigan from 1988 through 1990 under legendary coach Bo Schembechler .

Brady would arrive in Ann Arbor several years later, beginning his Michigan career in 1995. Vada Murray died in 2011 following a battle with lung cancer, and his daughter continues to honor him every time she takes the court.

Harper wears No.27 at Nebraska because it was her father’s number at Michigan. Her own career has already developed into an impressive one.

Murray earned first-team All-America honors as a junior last season and is a three-time first-team All-Big Ten selection. She has also become one of the most recognizable personalities in college volleyball, building a major social-media following alongside her success on the court.

Nebraska entered the matchup ranked No.1 in the country and backed up that status by sweeping No.2 Texas in straight sets. The victory left the Cornhuskers unbeaten through five matches without dropping a single set.

Brady’s daughter helped bring NFL legend courtside

Brady ’s appearance was not simply another celebrity sighting. Vivian has become increasingly serious about volleyball, and Murray believes that interest has helped draw Brady closer to the sport.

“I know his daughter's into the sport, so I'm sure that's how he got into it and grew a love for the game,” Murray said.

“I think it's awesome that we have people who are legends in their sport wanting to come and support a sport that's growing in the last few years and has been so popular. I think it's just really fun. I know our team loved that he was here.”

The viral embrace may have introduced Murray to a much wider audience, but she hardly needed the moment to establish herself. She is already an All-American, one of Nebraska’s most important players and a leading figure in a sport whose national profile continues to climb.

articles.summary: The Raiders rookie is taking an old-school approach to learning the NFL
articles.body:
Fernando Mendoza hasn't taken a regular-season snap for the Las Vegas Raiders yet, but the No. 1 overall pick is already displaying a habit that could play a major role in his development.

Mendoza is an obsessive note-taker, and he doesn't just jot things down when he's in the film room. He prefers writing by hand, carefully recording lessons and information that he can revisit later.

It's a routine he's followed since high school, when he would sometimes skip lunch with his classmates to spend extra time with his head coach preparing for practice.

That dedication has followed him into the NFL. Raiders quarterbacks coach Mike Sullivan has watched Mendoza document his progress and believes much of the young quarterback's confidence comes from the preparation behind his performance.

"[He] didn't have the neatest handwriting, but I appreciated him doing that. I said, 'Maybe you could type this next time,'" Raiders' quarterbacks coach Mike Sullivan told ESPN.

"But he went through that process, and he's someone that I think a lot of his confidence comes from the preparation and the type of time and effort that he puts in."

Mendoza even once brought the notebook along to a private brunch with Tom Brady and Travis Scott, where the conversation covered leadership, accountability, business and football. Mendoza wrote down the lessons he heard so he could review them afterward.

That approach could prove particularly useful as he adjusts to life in the NFL.

Why Mendoza's preparation could pay off

The Raiders aren't rushing Mendoza into action. Head coach Klint Kubiak has named Kirk Cousins the team's Week 1 starter against the Miami Dolphins, meaning Mendoza will begin his NFL career watching from the sideline.

That decision is frustrating for some fans. The Raiders haven't had a highly drafted quarterback generate this much anticipation in years, and there'll naturally be excitement about seeing what Mendoza can do.

However, the organization appears to believe that patience is the better option.

Cousins brings extensive NFL experience and familiarity with Kubiak's offensive system, making him a logical choice while Mendoza continues learning.

Mendoza doesn't need to win immediately. He needs to understand the offense, adjust to the speed of professional football and build the confidence necessary to eventually take control of the franchise.

Former Raiders quarterback Derek Carr has also supported the decision to give Mendoza additional time. His message to fans was essentially that they've waited this long and can afford to wait a little longer.

That's where Mendoza's note-taking habit could become especially important. Every practice rep, meeting and conversation can provide another lesson, while reviewing those handwritten notes gives him an opportunity to reinforce what he's learned.

Research has suggested that handwriting notes can improve learning and recall when they're actively reviewed, which fits Mendoza's approach particularly well.

Mendoza's willingness to learn and continually evaluate himself gives the Raiders an encouraging foundation.

articles.title: A veteran QB and an elderly owner: Inside the perfect storm that could send Maxx Crosby to Dallas
articles.standfirst: The Cowboys now have flexibility and history of interest to make another serious run at the Raiders pass rusher
articles.summary: The Cowboys now have flexibility and history of interest to make another serious run at the Raiders pass rusher
articles.body:
Dallas has spent much of the past year circling Maxx Crosby without ever completing a deal. Now, after the Cowboys created more than $30 million in salary-cap space, one FOX personality believes the long-running pursuit could finally end with the Raiders star in Texas.

Danny Parkins argued on First Things First that Dallas is entering exactly the kind of window in which sacrificing future draft capital can make sense.

The Cowboys have a veteran quarterback in Dak Prescott , an aging owner in Jerry Jones and a championship drought stretching back to the 1995 season.

“If they think they’re losing [George] Pickens next year, then that means that this team is the most talented team they should have for a few years,” Parkins said.

“And that’s the exact situation, especially when you add in veteran quarterback, owner in his early 80s, 30+ year Super Bowl drought. That’s the exact situation to mortgage a little bit of the future.

"Like trade a draft pick to go get a player. So I think Maxx Crosby’s gonna be a Cowboy.”

The prediction came after Dallas reportedly restructured contracts for Kenny Clark, DaRon Bland and Jake Ferguson , creating roughly $19 million in additional room.

Cowboys already tried to land Crosby

Crosby isn't a new name inside the Dallas rumor mill. The Cowboys previously explored deals for the five-time Pro Bowler, including talks with Las Vegas last season.

Their interest persisted into this year, when Crosby was again the subject of trade discussions before a potential move elsewhere reportedly fell apart following a physical.

That history matters because Dallas has already demonstrated a willingness to pay heavily for defensive help.

The Cowboys ultimately acquired Quinnen Williams in another major deal, but Crosby would fill a different need as a game-changing edge rusher.

He remains one of the NFL’s most productive defensive players, finishing last season with 10 sacks, 28 tackles for loss, 73 total tackles, two forced fumbles and an interception despite playing 15 games.

Former Bears linebacker Brian Urlacher has also suggested Dallas would find a way to make the finances work if Jones truly decided Crosby was the target.

“If they want him bad enough, Jerry will find a way to get him,” Urlacher said.

Las Vegas still controls biggest variable

Any move still depends on the Raiders becoming willing sellers. Crosby remains under contract with Las Vegas, and there is no indication that a trade is imminent.

The equation could change quickly, though, if the Raiders struggle again after finishing 3-14 last season.

Mike Florio of Pro Football Talk has suggested Las Vegas could eventually decide to “get value for him” rather than hold onto a star player through another losing season.

That scenario would likely put Dallas back in the conversation immediately.

The Cowboys have already added veteran Von Miller , but Crosby would give them a younger, elite pass rusher capable of changing the structure of the entire defense.

Dallas also owns future first-round capital it could use if the front office decides this roster is close enough to justify an aggressive move.

Parkins isn't predicting a minor deadline addition. He's predicting Dallas finally finishes a pursuit that has already survived multiple rounds of trade speculation.
